summary: Ireland runs its own visa policy: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens have freedom of movement, British citizens travel under the Common Travel Area, visitors from the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and many other countries need no visa and are admitted for up to 3 months at the immigration officer's discretion, and visa nationals apply for a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry).

Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Visas for Ireland
Citizens Information — Visa requirements for entering Ireland

fee.notes: €60 for single entry, €100 for multiple entry; some nationalities and categories are fee-exempt. Apply online via the AVATS system, then submit your passport and documents as instructed. Expect a decision within approximately 8 weeks of the application reaching the visa office, embassy or consulate.

passportValidity.text: If you need a visa for Ireland, your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave Ireland. No official source we could read states a validity rule for visa-exempt travellers.

travelInsurance.text: If your visa is approved, you must have evidence of medical or travel insurance when you arrive at the port of entry and present it to the immigration officer on request. For other visitors, the Immigration Service lists proof of health insurance covering the stay among the useful documents an officer may ask about.

onwardTicket.text: Not among the documents the Irish Immigration Service says you must present (passport, visa if needed, boarding card). It lists a travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, proof of health insurance and accommodation details among other useful documents an officer may ask about.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared to Customs when entering or leaving the EU at an Irish airport or port, including on journeys to or from the UK (but not Northern Ireland).

source.name: Revenue — Travelling with, or sending, cash

notes: Arriving from outside the EU, Revenue's duty-free allowances are goods worth up to €430 if you are 15 or over (€215 if under 15), plus 200 cigarettes (or 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco), 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres of drinks up to 22% alcohol, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer.

Revenue says that if you arrive from outside the EU with certain foodstuffs (mainly meat, milk, fish or products made from them), medicines, plants or animals, products of endangered species, or firearms, you must declare them to a customs officer.

safety.text: The UK government advises taking precautions against bag-snatching and pickpocketing, avoiding carrying valuables and large amounts of money, and locking your vehicle and parking in a secure car park where possible.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Ireland. Canada's travel advice notes that Ireland is subject to seasonal storms, windstorms and severe weather, and that heavy rains can cause flooding.

idp.text: Ireland is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The UK government says British and Irish citizens can travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area, and that some airlines and ferry operators require a passport as identification, so check your carrier's rules. Ireland's Immigration Service says visa-required nationals need an Irish visa unless they qualify under the British Irish Visa Scheme or the Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme.
Canada's travel advice says traffic drives on the left in Ireland, and that some roads can be uneven, narrow and winding, particularly in rural areas, and may become hazardous in severe weather.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or ETA for Ireland?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the Immigration Service's list of nationalities that do not need a visa for Ireland. On arrival the immigration officer decides how long you may stay, up to a maximum of 3 months, and stamps the date in your passport.

faq.question: Can I visit Ireland with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Not on its own. Ireland's Immigration Service bases the visa requirement on nationality, and visa-required nationals need an Irish short stay 'C' visa. The exceptions it lists are Chinese and Indian nationals living in China or India whose UK visa is endorsed "BIVS", and nationals of the Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme countries who have entered the UK on an eligible UK short-stay visa.

faq.question: Do I need a UK ETA to travel to Ireland?
faq.answer: No official Irish source we could read requires a UK ETA for travel to Ireland. Ireland's Immigration Service says a UK ETA cannot be used under its Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme: a visa-required national who holds a UK ETA rather than a UK visa needs a separate Irish visa.

faq.question: Do South African citizens need a visa for Ireland?
faq.answer: Yes. South Africa is on the Immigration Service's list of nationalities that need a visa for Ireland. South Africans apply for a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry) online through AVATS before travelling.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Ireland as a tourist?
faq.answer: The immigration officer decides how long you may stay, up to a maximum of 3 months, and stamps the date in your passport; visitors on a short stay 'C' visa must leave before that stamp expires.
